title: MvBody: Multi-View-Based Hybrid Transformer Using Optical 3D Body Scan for Explainable Cesarean Section Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2511.03212v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Accurately assessing the risk of cesarean section (CS) delivery is critical, especially in settings with limited medical resources, where access to healthcare is often restricted. Early and reliable risk prediction allows better-informed prenatal care decisions and can improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. However, most existing predictive models are tailored for in-hospital use during labor and rely on parameters that are often unavailable in resource-limited or home-based settings. In this study, we conduct a pilot investigation to examine the feasibility of using 3D body shape for CS risk assessment for future applications with more affordable general devices. We propose a novel multi-view-based Transformer network, MvBody, which predicts CS risk using only self-reported medical data and 3D optical body scans obtained between the 31st and 38th weeks of gestation. translated_title: MvBody：基于多视角的混合Transformer网络，利用光学3D人体扫描实现可解释的剖腹产预测
translated_abstract: 准确评估剖腹产（CS）分娩风险至关重要，尤其是在医疗资源有限的环境中，因为这些地区获得医疗保健的机会往往受限。早期可靠的风险预测有助于做出更明智的产前护理决策，并可改善孕产妇和新生儿的结局。然而，现有的大多数预测模型都是为住院分娩期间使用而设计的，依赖于在资源有限或居家环境中通常无法获得的参数。在本研究中，我们开展了一项试点研究，以检验利用3D体型进行剖腹产风险评估的可行性，以便未来能够使用更经济实惠的通用设备。我们提出了一种新颖的基于多视角的Transformer网络MvBody，该网络仅使用自我报告的医疗数据和在妊娠第31周至第38周之间获得的3D光学人体扫描来预测剖腹产风险。为了提高训练效率和模型在数据稀缺情况下的泛化能力（摘要不完整）……
tldr: 提出了一种基于多视角混合Transformer的MvBody模型，仅利用妊娠31-38周期间的3D光学人体扫描和自我报告医疗数据，即可实现可解释的剖腹产风险预测，适用于医疗资源有限的环境。
en_tdlr: MvBody, a novel multi-view-based hybrid Transformer network, enables explainable cesarean section risk prediction using only 3D optical body scans and self-reported medical data obtained between weeks 31-38 of gestation, making it feasible for resource-limited settings.
